title: AI's workday doubles every 7 months (METR time horizon)

scenes.text: In 2019, the best AI could handle three-second tasks. Today, twelve-hour ones.
METR measures it: how long a human expert takes on the tasks the AI completes half the time.
That length doubles roughly every seven months. And since 2023, every four.
Seconds with GPT-2, minutes with GPT-4, an hour in 2025… and twelve hours today.
But careful: that's succeeding half the time. Ask for 80%, and it drops to just over an hour.
And these are software tasks, cleaner than real work, with a huge margin of error: from 5 to 60 hours.
So don't ask whether AI can do your job. Ask which tasks, how many hours, and how reliably.
The stopwatch is the right instrument. But it's not a verdict.
Save it, and share it with someone who thinks AI has stalled.
